title: Tonbo Imaging Shares Jump 66% on Debut After IPO Subscribed 136 Times
excerpt: The Bengaluru defence electronics maker listed at Rs 1,162 against a Rs 700 issue price, in an entirely offer-for-sale IPO that brings the company itself no proceeds.
body:
• Tonbo Imaging listed at Rs 1,162 on the BSE on Friday, a 66% premium over its Rs 700 IPO price, and at Rs 1,160 on the NSE, up 65.71%.
  • The Rs 852.18 crore IPO was subscribed about 136 times and was entirely an offer for sale, so the company receives no proceeds from the issue.
  • The Bengaluru defence electronics maker has deployed over 28,000 tactical systems across 24 countries, spanning thermal imaging, weapon sights and missile seekers.
  • For investors: the listing gain came despite FY26 revenue falling 22.7% to Rs 362.6 crore and net profit falling about 30% to Rs 50.8 crore, so the premium prices in execution of delayed orders.

Shares of Tonbo Imaging India, a Bengaluru-based defence electronics maker, listed on Friday at Rs 1,162 on the BSE, a premium of 66% over the issue price of Rs 700. On the NSE the stock opened at Rs 1,160, a gain of 65.71%. The debut made Tonbo the clear winner among four companies listing the same day, even as the broader market traded lower.

Later in the session the stock eased from its listing price, trading at Rs 1,059.05 on the BSE, down 8.86% from the open but still 51.28% above the issue price. Market capitalisation at the listing price was about Rs 6,656 crore on the BSE, according to Inc42, while YourStory put capitalisation at Rs 6,191.91 crore on the BSE after the early pullback.

An offer for sale, heavily bid

The Rs 852.18 crore initial public offering was open from October 15 to October 19 at a price band of Rs 665-700 per share and was subscribed about 136 times, with bids for 115.87 crore shares against 85.26 lakh shares on offer. Qualified institutional buyers led demand. Ahead of the issue, the company raised Rs 255.4 crore from anchor investors, allotting 36.5 lakh shares to 43 investors at Rs 700 each, including SBI Mutual Fund, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock and WhiteOak Capital.

The issue comprised entirely an offer for sale of about 1.22 crore shares by promoters and existing shareholders, with no fresh issue component. Tonbo will therefore receive no proceeds; the money goes to the selling shareholders. Cofounders Arvind Lakshmikumar, Ankit Kumar and Cecilia D'Souza collectively sold shares worth Rs 137.2 crore, with Lakshmikumar accounting for Rs 80.5 crore.

What Tonbo makes

Tonbo designs and manufactures sensing, processing, communication and guidance systems for surveillance, reconnaissance, targeting and control. Its portfolio includes thermal imaging cores, weapon sights, targeting systems, missile seekers and fire control systems. As of June 30, 2026, the company said it had deployed over 28,000 tactical systems and served customers across 24 countries. It competes globally with firms such as Teledyne FLIR in the United States, Hensoldt in Germany and Controp in Israel in electro-optical and infrared systems.

The company was bought out from Sarnoff Corporation in 2012 by its promoters and pivoted from research services to designing advanced imaging and sensor systems for military use. It handles prototype development, system integration and qualification testing in-house and outsources manufacturing to partners including Kaynes Technology and Avalon Technology.

The numbers behind the premium

The strong listing came despite a weaker FY26. Operating revenue fell 22.7% year on year to Rs 362.6 crore from Rs 469.1 crore, and net profit declined about 30% to Rs 50.8 crore from Rs 72.8 crore. In the first quarter of FY27 the company reported a net loss of Rs 17.7 crore on operating revenue of Rs 36 crore. Chief executive Lakshmikumar attributed the FY26 decline to delays in executing international programmes, which pushed deliveries into FY27.

That sets the test for the stock after its debut pop. Investors who bought at the listing price are paying for order execution, margin recovery and cash flow, not for last year's results. On Friday the Sensex fell 409.06 points, or 0.56%, to 72,840.33 and the Nifty dropped 173.65 points, or 0.77%, to 22,514, which made Tonbo's premium stand out further against a falling market.
